subject: Redlines: liability framework — annualized vs contract-wide cap options
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Janet Lewis <janet@NimbusAnalytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-01 09:12:34 -0700
Subject: Liability framework — initial proposal and next steps

Janet — thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is our updated liability proposal (Redwood_Liability_Proposal_v3.pdf) that reflects two alternative approaches we discussed:

1) Annualized cap: rolling 12-month fee-based cap (common for bursty usage customers). Sample language: "Aggregate liability per rolling 12-month period shall not exceed the fees paid to Redwood under the Order Form during the immediately preceding 12 months."

2) Contract-wide cap: total cap equal to 3x fees paid during the Term. Sample language: "Aggregate liability shall not exceed three times the fees paid under the Agreement during the Term."

We also flagged carve-outs for: gross negligence/fraud, IP indemnities, and data breach-related regulatory fines (we propose carve-out for regulatory fines but include coverage for remediation costs up to the cap).

Quick ask: can you confirm whether your procurement/legal team has a hard requirement for contract-wide caps (vs annualized) or whether they will accept either with a preference? If they push for higher multipliers (e.g., unlimited for security), we should identify acceptable remediation language and potential SLA credits as mitigation.

Next steps: Monica, can you capture the two options in HubSpot and open the DocuSign packet depending on which direction they pick? Karthik, please propose fallback redline language for the security carve-out and a short negotiating playbook (bulleted).

Thanks,
Jonas

--

Date: 2026-07-02 10:04:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Liability framework — initial proposal and next steps

Jonas — appreciate the clear options and the PDF. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Our legal team typically prefers a contract-wide cap for enterprise agreements because our finance team wants one reconciliation point at renewal. They're open to discussing an annualized approach if the commercials are tighter (lower multiplier).
- For security incidents, our counsel is unlikely to accept a broad carve-out for regulatory fines; instead they want explicit coverage for customer remediation and indemnity for third-party claims resulting from Redwood's negligence.
- Consequential damages: we need language that doesn't eviscerate our remedies for lost analytics derived from the model (value-based losses). Can Redwood propose a limited consequential damages carve-in for data corruption caused by Redwood?

I'll loop in our procurement lead if we need to trade dollars for cap structure. For now, can you do three concrete options: (A) contract-wide 3x fees, (B) annualized 1.5x fees per rolling 12 months, (C) contract-wide 2x fees + expanded security indemnity? Put the options in a single doc so our counsel can pick.

Thanks — Janet

Janet Lewis
Head of Procurement, Nimbus Analytics
janet@NimbusAnalytics.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-07-03 08:45:11 -0700
Subject: RE: Liability framework — initial proposal and next steps

Folks — drafted the three-option table as requested. Attached is a short playbook in the Word redline (Nimbus_Redlines_Liability.docx) but I summarized below: 

Option A — Contract-wide 3x fees:
- Pros: tidy reconciliation at expiry, aligns with enterprise finance ask.
- Cons: larger one-time exposure; harder to defend for multi-year high-spend customers.
- Negotiation levers: limits on consequential damages (narrow definition), add SLA credit schedule for availability incidents to reduce exposure.

Option B — Annualized 1.5x rolling 12 months:
- Pros: caps exposure in any 12-month window, better for rapid-growth customers with spiky usage.
- Cons: finance dislike; operationally more complex.
- Negotiation levers: allow annual reset with reporting; provide visibility dashboard and cost-smoothing credits.

Option C — Contract-wide 2x fees + expanded security indemnity:
- Pros: balances finance comfort and stronger allocation for security events.
- Cons: Redwood bears more risk on security; require clear definition of "security incident caused by Redwood's breach" and a cure window.

Carve-outs / Definitions to propose: 
- "Consequential damages" narrowly defined to exclude loss of profits only where they arise from data corruption caused directly by Redwood's negligence; otherwise preserved.
- "Regulatory fines" treated as excluded from cap only where Redwood is found by a court or regulator to have acted with gross negligence or willful misconduct.

I'll attach language snippets and suggested redlines. Jonas — suggest we present the three options to Janet with recommended Redwood posture: we prefer Option B for technical fit but recognize the customer's finance bias to Option A; default fallback to Option C if security indemnity is demanded.

-Karthik

Team — thanks for the clear options and playbook. Procurement prefers Option A (contract-wide 3x) as the starting point. Two asks before we move to signatures: 

1) Can Redwood narrow the consequential damages carve-out to permit recovery where there is provable data corruption caused by Redwood? Sample clause: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, consequential damages arising directly from verifiable data corruption caused by Redwood's gross negligence shall be recoverable up to the aggregate liability cap."

2) On security/regulatory fines: our counsel will accept the proposed court/regulator finding threshold but asks for a reciprocal cooperation obligation for forensic investigations and a defined escrow for remediation costs (or a cap on Redwood's remediation spend).

If you can accept those two refinements in the packet we can fast-track. Otherwise, we'll escalate to our CFO for a tradeoff on commercials. Janet

--
